description: EMBOSS 6.6.0 est2genome (Richard Mott's est_genome, embest.c): the spliced alignment of EST sequences (a FASTA text, every record is aligned) to an unspliced genomic sequence (the first record of a FASTA text). A local alignment with introns: matches +match, mismatches -mismatch, a base deleted from either sequence -gapPenalty, an intron of any length -intronPenalty, or -splicePenalty when it starts after a donor and ends on an acceptor site (usesplice, default true: GT/AG for a forward gene, CT/AC for a reversed gene). mode 'both' (default) aligns the forward and the reverse-complemented EST with forward-gene splice sites, then repeats the better one with reversed-gene splice sites and reports the best (the Note line tells which: forward est / reversed est, forward / REVERSED GENE); 'forward' and 'reverse' (case-insensitive, unique abbreviations) align one strand. An alignment is written when its score is at least minScore: the Exon lines (score, percent identity, genomic and EST coordinates, names, EST description), the +Intron / -Intron / ?Intron lines, the Span line and, after a blank line, the Segment lines; with align the alignment itself (introns as their first and last five bases and their length, > forward / < reversed splice direction) in blocks of width columns and 'Alignment Score'. reverse prints the coordinates of a reversed EST on its original strand; best = false (-nobest) also writes the other alignment (with a single strand mode the program crashes: refused with InvalidOperationException); space is the megabytes of the matrix above which the linear-space divide and conquer is used (raised to 1.5e-6 x genome length with a warning in messages); shuffle > 0 sets minScore to the best score + 1 (the program's shuffle does not change the sequence); seed has no effect; width of 0 or less with align never ends in the program (refused). Negative penalties are used as their absolute values. sequenceQualifiers: EMBOSS sequence qualifiers after the files (-sbegin1 5 -send1 90 -sreverse1 for the ESTs, -sbegin2 ... for the genomic sequence). Byte for byte equal to est2genome on 330 runs (forward / reverse genes, ESTs on either strand, every option, the linear-space recursion, the crashes).

estFasta.description: The EST sequences as FASTA text (-estsequence); every record is aligned.

genomeFasta.description: The genomic sequence as FASTA text (-genomesequence); the first record is used.

match.description: Score for matching two bases (-match, default 1).

mismatch.description: Cost for mismatching two bases (-mismatch, default 1).

gapPenalty.description: Cost for deleting a single base in either sequence, excluding introns (-gappenalty, default 2).

intronPenalty.description: Cost for an intron, independent of length (-intronpenalty, default 40).

splicePenalty.description: Cost for an intron between a donor and an acceptor site (-splicepenalty, default 20).

minScore.description: Exclude alignments with scores below this threshold (-minscore, default 30).

reverse.description: Report the coordinates of a reversed EST on the original strand (-reverse, default false).

useSplice.description: Use donor and acceptor splice sites (-usesplice, default true).

best.description: Print only the best alignment (-best, default true; false = -nobest).

space.description: Space threshold in megabytes for the linear-space recursion (-space, default 10.0).

seed.description: Random number seed (-seed, default 20825; no effect on the output).

sequenceQualifiers.description: EMBOSS sequence qualifiers as typed after the files: -sbegin1 5 -send1 90 -sreverse1 -slower1 -supper1 (input 1 = the ESTs) and -sbegin2 ... (input 2 = the genomic sequence). The text is resolved exactly as the EMBOSS program resolves it on its command line after the sequence arguments (ACD, 6.6.0): -sbegin1 3, -sbegin1=3, -nosreverse1, -sreverse1 N, any case, -/--/ prefix, and every UNIQUE abbreviation (-sbeg1, -sre2; uniqueness is decided among all qualifiers of the program, an ambiguous or unknown one is refused). The number is the sequence (1, and 2 for the second sequence of a two-sequence program; 1 for a program with one sequence). An unnumbered qualifier belongs to the LAST sequence given (-sbegin 3 is -sbegin2 3 in a two-sequence program) until a qualifier of another sequence ends that tie; after that it applies to all sequences. -sformat selects the file format of the text; -ufo -fformat -fopenfile name the feature file of a program that takes the features of its sequences (diffseq: the files are given by the tool); -sask -squick -sdbname -sid -iquery are accepted without effect (residue strings have no file); any other qualifier or a stray word is refused.

messages.description: What the program writes to standard error (the space warning).

errors.message: The EST sequences cannot be empty
est2genome: 'x' is not a valid menu option (both, forward, reverse).
est2genome: segmentation fault (-nobest with a single strand mode)
